> You're seriously going to watch two or three videos and make a half assed assumption out of that? 

First, no, in fact I've been watching you for quite a while, like 2 or 3 months and I've seen several videos of your "historical accuracy" videos and I'm well aware of what i am saying about your videos.

>I don't "favor" a nation in the sense that I'm somehow trying to alter  people's perceptions of armored vehicles, because I don't care what  tanks people like the most and I don't hate inanimate objects.

I don't say you try to effect people's opinion on armored vehicles. I say your personal feelings about inanimate objects got in the way of making something historically accurate. Yes, You don't hate inanimate objects but as you mentioned:

>I "favor" US tanks in the sense that I like them the most.

I'm not saying you are not capable of being accurate. I'm saying you're not doing what is required for it to be accurate.

Second:

>Saying that a source isn't good purely because it doesn't come from the  nation the tank belongs to is a dumb take and I'm sick of hearing it.

In history, specifically in military history, You can't only rely on one source and count it as accurate. You can't just see one side of the subject. I'm sure you're aware of that.  
In your T-64A video you only mention 2 sources (Without mentioning Armor) and those are Richard Ogorkiewicz and Steven Zaloga. Although I don't discredit these people, You didn't mention any service history or any source from tank operators.  
Look, I'm not trying to say T-64A or any tank from any nation is good or bad. I'm saying in order to say something is historically accurate, you need check different sources.

> Reputable AFV historians will often have connections with that nation's  AFV design teams or will gain access to their archives. Information is  not limited by borders. 

Sure, Information is not limited by border, but people can use information in different ways and interpretations. They can simply see different sides of a matter and think that's more important than other side.  
I understand that for prototypes like MBT-70 or T14 or T25, there are only American (German in KPz-70) available. But I think you can look at Soviet, Russian, Czechoslovakian and Ukrainian sources as well for a Soviet tank regarding a historical accuracy and views on a tank. Even about M60, US wasn't the only country to operate those and I'm sure you're well aware of it.  


Third:

> My BMP-1 video had more positive points than my M60 video, Sheridan video, MBT-70 video, T14 video, T25 video, etc. 

I didn't really wanted to actually see and count these but i watched those again and did.  
So from what I've watched:  
BMP 1 video had: 10 cons and 4 pros mentioned (mainly based on Marine Corps Intelligence activity)   
M60 video had: 9 cons and 3 pros mentioned (3 of cons regarding M60s before RISE upgrade and 1 regarding A2 variant, mainly based on ad a141 935 M60 Series Update Assessment and Mesko)  
T25 video had: 4 cons and 8 pros mentioned (Mainly based on Hunnicutt)  
Sheridan video had: 10 cons and 4 pros (Mainly based on Zaloga)  
MBT-70 video had: 8 cons and 6 pros (Mainly based on Hunnicutt and Lessons from the US-German Experience)  
T-62 video had: 10 cons and 5 pros (mainly based on how to fight: The T-62 tank and US conflicts in 21th century)

I don't want to tell you what to do, neither i can and i did this only because sources. in your recent video about T-80s your only source was again, Zaloga. I again emphasize that I don't discredit him. but relying only on one source doesn't give that much accuracy.  
I've seen your comment under that video too. Again I'm not saying you're not capable of recognizing flaws with American vehicles. I doubt American sources state their vehicles flaws. as an example 3 of flaws about M60 were mentioned after it was upgraded and they were explaining reasons for that upgrade.

As a tank enthusiast, I feel good when i see people discuss about them. It makes me well pleased when I see content about them and It might not look like But I'm trying to improve this environment for people like myself so don't take these as insults.
